Subject: Deployment & data residency: Hosted vs Private (EU/APAC) - follow up

Hi Karim,

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Finovate Bank preference: EU-only data residency for production workloads; potential APAC presence later for regional offices.
- Primary use case: document ingestion + chat assistants (high QPS, low latency for Lisbon and London users).
- Options we discussed: Hosted API (EU region), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools in EU), Private deployment (VPC or on-prem).

Questions we flagged for you to confirm:
1) Is EU-only a hard requirement for all production data (including logs/KV cache), or is cross-region replication for DR acceptable if data is encrypted and stays within our contract controls?
2) Do you have a preference for VPC-hosted vs fully on-prem (hardware procurement timelines differ substantially)?

Next steps from Redwood:
- I'll loop in Aditya (solutions engineering) for region & latency guidance and Marissa for procurement/pricing.
- Attached a short deployment options summary and our current EU region availability spreadsheet.

Would you be available for a 30-min technical follow-up tomorrow at 10:00 AM GMT to walk constraints and handoffs?

Thanks,
Lauren

Hi Lauren,

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from Finovate Bank: 

- EU-only for all production data is a firm requirement. That includes logs and any persisted caches.
- For DR, we can consider cross-region read replicas within the EU (e.g., eu-west-1 -> eu-central-1), but we cannot replicate outside EU for production data.
- Regarding deployment mode: our security team prefers VPC-hosted private deployments (customer VPC peering to Redwood Dedicated/Private control plane). On-prem is possible but would add significant procurement lead time (~6-9 months).

We'd like Aditya to give us a short note on how latency looks from Lisbon/London into EU-hosted endpoints versus a private VPC option and any constraints around KV cache residency. Also, can you confirm SOC2 documentation and whether audit logs can be forwarded to our SIEM?

Karim Rahman

Subject: Re: Deployment & data residency: Hosted vs Private (EU/APAC) - follow up

Hi Karim, looping in from solutions engineering. Short technical answers below: 

1) EU-only production: yes, we can guarantee that token payloads, request/response logs, and KV cache persistence stay within EU regions when you choose a Private VPC or Dedicated capacity pinned to EU. For Hosted API, we offer EU region endpoints (eu-west-1) but customers who need contractual EU-only guarantees typically choose Dedicated or Private so we can bind routing and storage at the tenant level.

2) Cross-region DR within EU: supported. We can configure async replication between EU regions (eu-west-1 <-> eu-central-1) with encryption in transit and at rest.

3) Latency: from Lisbon/London to eu-west-1 hosted API you're looking at median 12-25ms per token for request/response roundtrips (app-level latency will be higher). Private VPC peered into our EU Dedicated nodes will typically shave 5-10ms depending on routing and whether you terminate TLS on your side. We can run a quick traceroute/ping during the follow-up call.

4) KV cache residency: when running Dedicated or Private, KV stores are provisioned in the selected region and not replicated outside region unless configured for DR. Hosted API will use shared multi-tenant caches in the region unless you purchase a dedicated cache product.

5) SOC2 & audit logs: SOC2 report (redacted) attached; we also support forwarding audit logs to your SIEM via secure delivery (S3 bucket with encryption or direct SIEM integration).

6) Timeline & next steps: for a VPC-hosted private deployment we estimate a 6-8 week onboarding (network setup, peering, IAM config, pilot). On-prem is 4-6 months. If you want, we can start with a hosted EU canary for faster time-to-value and then migrate to Dedicated/VPC for production.

I'll attach the EU region availability sheet and a short matrix comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC private options. Happy to join the 10:00 AM GMT slot tomorrow.

- Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
